messages:
Maya (Support): FYI - ACME reported a partial outage after they tried to rotate their API credentials. They rotated vault/KMS last night and after that ~15% of their jobs started returning 403s to our /v1/generate endpoint. Handoff to infra/SRE to triage. Root info below. @Chris @Diego

ACME-SRE: Repro steps:
1) Update Vault secret at secret/data/acme/redwood with new token
2) Vault agent sidecar (kv-v2) is configured to expose REDWOOD_API_KEY as env at container start
3) Rolling deploy of app (didn't drain nodes) -> some pods get 403s: {"error":"permission_denied","message":"API key invalid or missing scope"}
4) header seen: Authorization: Bearer rk_newABcd... and X-Api-Key-Id: key_66f1a

Chris (Infra): Can you share the X-Api-Key-Id and any trace id from our edge? Need to see whether key_66f1a is active in our system and whether signature verification failed.

ACME-SRE: Trace id trc-9f2d4e5a, key id key_66f1a. They attached a packet capture (redacted first 8 chars): Authorization: Bearer rk_66f1aXx...

Diego (SRE): Pulled the trace: trc-9f2d4e5a shows auth-service -> verify_key() returned mismatch and logged signature_mismatch for key_66f1a. Downstream we responded 403. This smells like the key id mapping was not updated to match the secret material they injected.

Chris (Infra): Quick DB check: SELECT key_id,status,created_at FROM api_keys WHERE key_id='key_66f1a'; -> key_66f1a active created_at=2026-12-10T18:02:03Z. So platform considers it active. If auth-service expects a different raw token value for that key_id, HMAC won't match.

ACME-SRE: We didn't call Redwood's rotate endpoint. We just rewrapped the plaintext with a new KMS key and wrote the ciphertext into Vault. We thought replacing the secret in Vault would be enough.

Diego (SRE): That's the gap: rewrapping on customer's KMS/Vault doesn't automatically create or update a Redwood API key_id mapping. Our key_id is minted on-platform. If they replaced the token value but kept the same key_id header, requests will fail. Partial success suggests some pods had either the old token or a different copy of the secret.

ACME-SRE: We also noticed pods on two nodes kept returning the old env var. Kubelet logs show vault-agent reported "cached value present (age 2h)" and the init container copy step didn't overwrite existing files on disk for pods that were recreated quickly.

Chris (Infra): Two vectors to explain partial failures: 1) Vault agent caching + our agent's TTL meant some sidecars returned stale values to containers; 2) Their init-copy pattern keeps old files on node filesystem under certain race conditions. Combined with not draining nodes, few pods continued to present mismatched tokens.

Maya (Support): Immediate remediation we suggested:
- Create a new Redwood key via POST /v1/keys and update Vault with the new plaintext OR call /v1/keys/rotate for key_66f1a to have platform rotate bindings.
- Perform a full rollout: kubectl rollout restart deployment or drain affected nodes to force pods to be scheduled elsewhere and fetch fresh secret files.
- Verify Vault agent TTL and switch to a more aggressive refresh or use CSI-projected secrets.

ACME-SRE: Did a full rollout + node drain. Failures dropped to 0. They want a short root-cause note and a mitigation checklist.

Diego (SRE): Draft root cause:
- Customer replaced secret material in external KMS/Vault without coordinating with Redwood key lifecycle. Our platform associates a key_id with platform-side token material; changing customer-side ciphertext doesn't update that mapping.
- Some pods continued to run with stale secret copies due to Vault agent caching and their init-container copy method; race when replacement and pod restarts overlapped.

Chris (Infra): Long-term mitigations proposed to customer:
- Always rotate via Redwood API when you need a new API token or use our rotate endpoint to keep key_id consistent.
- Consider Vault dynamic secrets or a regeneration flow that calls our API as part of rotation orchestration.
- Use a secret mount method that supports live update (CSI driver) or ensure processes re-read secrets on SIGHUP; avoid one-time init-copy if you need in-place updates.
- Add verification smoke test post-rotation: curl our endpoint with new token and assert 200 before decommissioning old token.

Sean (PM): Customer requested an early-warning alert: if verify_key signature_mismatch increases for a given key_id, notify owner via webhook/email. Agree this is useful. We can track verify_key.signature_mismatch{key_id} and add a low-priority backlog item.

Chris (Infra): Internal action items:
- Chris: Update runbook with rotation checklist and sample curl commands and Vault update snippets (ETA EOD).
- Diego: Add auth-service metric for signature_mismatch per key_id and hook into alerting (ETA 72h).
- Sean: Create product backlog ticket for owner webhook/automation (sprint planning).

Maya (Support): Customer confirmed resolved after full rollout. Logging closure here. Will reopen if it reoccurs. Thanks all. :tada:

infra-oncall: Note: if you see partial 403s after customer rotates secrets, first ask for key_id + trace id, check signature_mismatch metric, and request node-level checks (drain/reschedule).

vault-bot: KV v2 info: secret/data/acme/redwood versions: [4,5]. last_write: 2026-12-11T01:05:00Z

Maya (Support): Closing: created runbook PR link will be posted. Customer to follow recommended rotation via Redwood API next time.
